context.title: The Northern Tribes
context.summary: Brief genealogies cover Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim and Asher, often counting their fighting men. A short story tells of grief in Ephraim's family.
context.background: The counts of 'mighty men of valour' look like military registers. Zebulun is missing and Dan is barely hinted at, and no one knows for certain why. Ephraim's line ends with Joshua, who led Israel into the land (v. 27, 'Jehoshua').

customs.note: Ephraim names his son Beriah, which sounds like the Hebrew for 'in evil' or 'in trouble,' marking the family's tragedy.

watchFor: Sherah, a woman, is credited with building three towns (v. 24).
Ephraim's mourning for sons killed by the men of Gath (vv. 21–22).

people.name: Issachar
people.summary: Hired (Gen. 30:18). “God hath given me,” said Leah, “my hire (Heb. sekhari)...and she called his name Issachar.” He was Jacob’s ninth son, and was born in Padan-aram (comp. 28:2).

people.name: Tola
people.summary: Eldest son of Issachar (Gen. 46:13).

people.name: Jashub
people.summary: The third of Issachar’s four sons (1 Chr. 7:1); called also Job (Gen. 46:13).

people.name: Puah
people.summary: The sons of Issachar.

people.name: Shimron
people.summary: Watchman, the fourth son of Issachar (Gen. 46:13; 1 Chr. 7:1; R.V., correctly, “Shimron”).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Uzzi
people.summary: A grandson of Issachar (1 Chr. 7:2, 3).

people.name: Rephaiah
people.summary: Head of the family.

people.name: Shemuel
people.summary: A prince of the tribe of Issachar (1 Chr. 7:2).

people.name: Michael
people.summary: 1 Chr. 7:3, a chief of the tribe of Issachar.

people.name: Obadiah
people.summary: A chief of the tribe of Issachar (1 Chr. 7:3).

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Bela
people.summary: The eldest son of Benjamin (Num. 26:38; “Belah,” Gen. 46:21).

people.name: Jediael
people.summary: One of the sons of Benjamin, whose descendants numbered 17,200 warriors (1 Chr. 7:6, 10, 11).

people.name: Jerimoth
people.summary: One of the sons of Bela (1 Chr. 7:7).

people.name: Uzzi
people.summary: A son of Bela, and grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:7).

people.name: Uzziel
people.summary: A son of Bela, and grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:7).

people.name: Abiah
people.summary: One of the sons of Becher, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:8).

people.name: Alameth
people.summary: One of the nine sons of Becher, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:8).

people.name: Anathoth
people.summary: Son of Becher.

people.name: Eliezer
people.summary: The son of Becher, and grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:8).

people.name: Elioenai
people.summary: Descendant of David.

people.name: Jerimoth
people.summary: Warrior of David.

people.name: Omri
people.summary: Sixth king of Israel.

people.name: Zemira
people.summary: Vine-dresser, a Benjamite; one of the sons of Becher (1 Chr. 7:8).

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: Jediael.

people.name: Bilhan
people.summary: Son of Jediael.

people.name: Chenaanah
people.summary: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 7:10).

people.name: Ehud
people.summary: A descendant of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:10), his great-grandson.

people.name: Jeush
people.summary: A son of Bilhan, grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:10).

people.name: Zethan
people.summary: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 7:10).

people.name: Shuppim
people.summary: The descendant of Ir.

people.name: Hushim
people.summary: The children of Dan.

people.name: Naphtali
people.summary: My wrestling, the fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid (Gen. 30:8). When Jacob went down into Egypt, Naphtali had four sons (Gen. 46:24).

people.name: Bilhah
people.summary: Faltering; bashful, Rachel’s handmaid, whom she gave to Jacob (Gen. 29:29). She was the mother of Dan and Naphtali (Gen. 30:3-8). Reuben was cursed by his father for committing adultry with her (35:22; 49:4).

people.name: Guni
people.summary: Son of Naphtali.

people.name: Jahzeel
people.summary: Allotted by God, the first of the sons of Naphtali (Gen. 46:24).

people.name: Manasseh
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1).

people.name: Machir
people.summary: Manasseh’s oldest son (Josh. 17:1), or probably his only son (see 1 Chr. 7:14, 15; comp. Num. 26:29-33; Josh. 13:31). His descendants are referred to under the name of Machirites, being the offspring of Gilead (Num. 26:29).

people.name: Gilead
people.summary: Son of Manasseh.

people.name: Zelophehad
people.summary: First-born, of the tribe of Manasseh, and of the family of Gilead; died in the wilderness. Having left no sons, his daughters, concerned lest their father’s name should be “done away from among his family,” made an appeal to Moses, who, by divine direction, appointed it as “a statute of judgment” in Israel that daughters should inherit their father’s portion when no sons were left (Num. 27:1-11).

people.name: Maachah
people.summary: Pressed down; worn; fastened.

people.name: Ulam
people.summary: Son of Manasseh.

people.name: Sheresh
people.summary: Root, a descendant of Manasseh (1 Chr. 7:16).

people.name: Bedan
people.summary: Deliverer of Israelites.

people.name: Abiezer
people.summary: Brother to to Ishhod and Mahlah.

people.name: Hammoleketh
people.summary: The queen, the daughter of Machir and sister of Gilead (1 Chr. 7:17, 18).

people.name: Shechem
people.summary: Son of Hamor the Hivite.

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

people.name: Shuthelah
people.summary: Son of Ephraim.

people.name: Bered
people.summary: A son of Shuthelah, and grandson of Ephraim (1 Chr. 7:20).

people.name: Tahath
people.summary: Son of Korah.

people.name: Tahath
people.summary: Son, Tahath his son.

people.name: Shuthelah
people.summary: Brother of Zebad.

people.name: Beriah
people.summary: A son of Ephraim (1 Chr. 7:20-23), born after the slaughter of his brothers, and so called by his father “because it went evil with his house” at that time.

people.name: Tahan
people.summary: His son,.

people.name: Ammihud
people.summary: The father of the Ephraimite chief Elishama, at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:10; 2:18; 7:48, 53).

people.name: Elishama
people.summary: A prince of Benjamin, grandfather of Joshua (Num. 1:10; 1 Chr. 7:26).

people.name: Laadan
people.summary: Son of Tahan.

people.name: Joshua
people.summary: Jehovah is his help, or Jehovah the Saviour. The son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, the successor of Moses as the leader of Israel.

people.name: Nun
people.summary: Beyond the fact that he was the father of Joshua nothing more is known of him (Ex. 33:11).

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 30:23, 24), who, on the occasion of his birth, said, “God hath taken away [Heb. ‘asaph] my reproach.”

people.name: Asher
people.summary: Happy, Jacob’s eigth son; his mother was Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid (Gen. 30:13). Of the tribe founded by him nothing is recorded beyond its holding a place in the list of the tribes (35:26; 46:17; Ex. 1:4, etc.) It increased in numbers twenty-nine percent, during the thirty-eight years’ wanderings.

people.name: Beriah
people.summary: One of Asher’s four sons, and father of Heber (Gen. 46:17).

people.name: Imnah
people.summary: The first-born of Asher.

people.name: Serah
people.summary: Abundance; princess, the daughter of Asher and grand-daughter of Jacob (Gen. 46:17); called also Sarah (Num. 26:46; R.V., “Serah”).

people.name: Heber
people.summary: Son of Beriah and grandson of Asher (Gen. 46:17; 1 Chr. 7:31, 32).

people.name: Hotham
people.summary: A stroke, great-grandson of Asher (1 Chr. 7:35).

people.name: Shamer
people.summary: A man of Asher (1 Chr. 7:32); called also Shamer (34).

people.name: Shua
people.summary: A daughter of Heber the Asherite (1 Chr. 7:32).

people.name: Pasach
people.summary: Clearing, one of the sons of Japhlet, of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:33).

people.name: Ahi
people.summary: Son of Shamer.

people.name: Zophah
people.summary: Spreading out, a son of Helem (1 Chr. 7:35), a chief of Asher.

people.name: Harnepher
people.summary: A chief of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:36).

people.name: Bezer
people.summary: A descendant of Asher (1 Chr. 7:37).

people.name: Jephunneh
people.summary: One of the descendants of Asher (1 Chr. 7:38).

people.name: Haniel
people.summary: A chief of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:39).

places.name: Gath
places.summary: A wine-vat, one of the five royal cities of the Philistines (Josh. 13:3) on which the ark brought calamity (1 Sam. 5:8, 9; 6:17). It was famous also as being the birthplace or residence of Goliath (1 Sam. 17:4).

places.name: Beth-horon
places.summary: House of the hollow, or of the cavern, the name of two towns or villages (2 Chr. 8:5; 1 Chr. 7:24) in the territory of Ephraim, on the way from Jerusalem to Joppa.

places.name: Bethel
places.summary: A place in Central Palestine, about 10 miles north of Jerusalem, at the head of the pass of Michmash and Ai. It was originally the royal Canaanite city of Luz (Gen. 28:19).

places.name: Gezer
places.summary: A precipice, an ancient royal Canaanitish city (Josh. 10:33; 12:12). It was allotted with its suburbs to the Kohathite Levites (21:21; 1 Chr. 6:67).

places.name: Naaran
places.summary: Boyish, juvenile, a town in Ephraim between Bethel and Jericho (1 Chr. 7:28).

places.name: Shechem
places.summary: A city in Samaria (Gen. 33:18), called also Sichem (12:6), Sychem (Acts 7:16). It stood in the narrow sheltered valley between Ebal on the north and Gerizim on the south, these mountains at their base being only some 500 yards apart.

places.name: Beth-shean
places.summary: House of security or rest, a city which belonged to Manasseh (1 Chr. 7:29), on the west of Jordan. The bodies of Saul and his sons were fastened to its walls.

places.name: Dor
places.summary: Dwelling, the Dora of the Romans, an ancient royal city of the Canaanites (Josh. 11:1, 2; 12:23). It was the most southern settlement of the Phoenicians on the coast of Syria.

places.name: Megiddo
places.summary: Place of troops, originally one of the royal cities of the Canaanites (Josh. 12:21), belonged to the tribe of Manasseh (Judg. 1:27), but does not seem to have been fully occupied by the Israelites till the time of Solomon (1 Kings 4:12; 9:15).

places.name: Taanach
places.summary: A sandy place, an ancient royal city of the Canaanites, on the south-western border of the plain of Esdraelon, 4 miles south of Megiddo. Its king was conquered by Joshua (12:21).
